id.description: Citation marker as it appears in the paper (e.g. '1', '12', 'Smith2020')

authors.description: Author names in 'Last, First' format (e.g. 'Vaswani, Ashish'). For single-name authors, use the name as-is.

relation.description: How this reference relates to the citing paper, judged from in-text citation context.

roles.description: Functional relation(s) this reference plays for the citing paper, drawn from the same vocabulary as the unit-graph edges; one or more. builds_on=a direct predecessor THIS paper's contribution builds on, improves, or extends (the cited method your work descends from); uses=a method/architecture/algorithm/technique/tool/dataset/benchmark reused as a building block, not the contribution's lineage; compares_to=compared against experimentally (a baseline) or critiqued/disagreed with (the `stance` field carries supportive/neutral/critical); background=field/concept context, motivation, future-work mention, or passing related mention. builds_on/uses/compares_to each reconcile to the unit-graph edge of the same name; background carries no edge and is never emitted as an entry. Do NOT emit background-only references at all — skip them; they stay in the verbatim bibliography blob. When ambiguous between builds_on and background, prefer builds_on if the cited work is plausibly a direct predecessor (high recall). A cited work whose own method or artifact is the thing compared (a system row/curve in a results table, a dataset row in a property/spec comparison) or that is explicitly argued against is compares_to; a work cited as the substrate the experiments run on or as the source of data, labels, or an evaluation protocol this paper follows, or a tool/theorem invoked at a method, setup, or proof step, is uses; but a citation whose only role is apparatus (an optimizer, sampler, metric-scoring model, hardware, or incidental tool/library) is background, not uses, and is skipped.

stance.description: How the citing paper positions itself: critical if the paper critiques or contrasts the work; supportive if it explicitly endorses or adopts the work's approach as its own foundation (or roles includes builds_on); otherwise neutral (plain usage of a resource, plain baseline). Default neutral.

salience.description: central = load-bearing for this paper's argument or experiments (a main baseline, a core building block, or relied on repeatedly); peripheral = structurally linked but minor; main baselines and the primary systems/datasets the paper's experiments run on are central, not peripheral.

provides_name.description: For builds_on, uses, and compares_to, the single most specific named artifact the citing paper takes from or compares against this work (e.g. 'Transformer', 'ImageNet', 'BERT'). Empty string when no concrete artifact is named. An apparatus name (an optimizer, sampler, metric-scoring model, or incidental tool/library) does not qualify: such a citation is background and is skipped.

provides_unit_ids.description: Always output an empty array []. Links to spine unit IDs are filled deterministically by the pipeline after section extraction; never populate this yourself.
